ambiguities.description: Tax ID is explicitly stated NOT to be a unique identifier for vendors (duplicates exist, parent-subsidiary same tax ID). It is retained as an attribute but should not be modeled with a uniqueness constraint. Confirm no external uniqueness applies.

source_references.excerpt: And could you identify a vendor by tax ID instead? ... You'd think so, but no. We have vendors with the same tax ID

ambiguities.description: The term 'tier' is heavily overloaded: Procurement's spend tier (bronze/silver/gold) vs Compliance's risk tier (low/medium/high) are two distinct fields that are both colloquially called 'tier', causing confusion in meetings. Modeled as two separate value types/fact types (VendorSpendTier, VendorRiskTier), but naming ambiguity in the business persists and should be flagged.

source_references.excerpt: And you both call it "tier." ... We both call it tier and it causes genuine chaos.

ambiguities.description: The 'preferred vendor' flag tracked informally by Mei in a spreadsheet is explicitly called ad hoc with no defined rule or process, and the facilitator/Mei agreed not to model it. Flagging that this exists as an unmodeled business practice that may need future capture if formalized.

source_references.excerpt: There's a column called "preferred." ... It's ad hoc. Don't model it.

ambiguities.description: The post-suspension handling of in-flight purchase orders (e.g., a possible 'run-off' status) is explicitly unresolved and pending a policy decision by the sourcing steering group. No constraint or additional status should be modeled yet, but this is a known gap.

source_references.excerpt: This goes to the sourcing steering group. It's a policy call, not a modeling call, and Legal has to be in the room.

ambiguities.description: Vendor addresses are mentioned as three distinct addresses (remit-to, ship-from, legal) that are 'frequently different and frequently wrong', but the transcript does not clarify whether these are three separate value types/roles or one Address concept with a type role. Granularity of Address (single text vs structured street/city/etc.) is also unclear.

source_references.excerpt: Address, though we have three addresses really -- remit-to, ship-from, and the legal one, which are frequently different and frequently wrong.

ambiguities.description: Whether the risk review 'signed off' status is a boolean flag, a date, or a person recorded is unclear -- the transcript mentions 'who signed it and when' but doesn't clarify the exact fields beyond review ID. This affects whether Reviewer/SignOffDate should be separate value types.

source_references.excerpt: It has a review ID, because we need to know who signed it and when, and auditors ask.

ambiguities.description: It is unclear whether vendor status history (draft->active->suspended transitions) needs temporal tracking (e.g., when did a vendor become active, how many times suspended) since the model as captured only reflects current-state status, not a history of transitions.

source_references.excerpt: Draft, active, suspended. ... Every vendor is in exactly one of them.

ambiguities.description: Whether the four regions (EMEA, APAC, NA, LATAM) are fixed forever or might change (splitting EMEA) is uncertain -- treated as a value constraint here but stakeholders note the list may evolve.

source_references.excerpt: Region code. EMEA, APAC, NA, LATAM. ... Four today. There's been talk of splitting EMEA but it hasn't happened.
